title: ∂C = 0 and x ∧ C⃗ = 0 a.e. imply that C annihilates Euler–Lie derivatives of test forms (core of Simon 6.2.33)
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) with C = τ(M, θ, ξ) (R.Represents C). Assume ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e. in the sense that for R.measure-a.e. x, ξ(x)(α.curryLeft x) = 0 for every (n+1)-covector α. Then C(γ) = 0 for all test forms β, γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with γ(y) = n·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y] for every y (Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y); that is, C annihilates the Lie derivative L_Xβ = d(ι_Xβ) + ι_X dβ of every test form along the Euler field X(y) = y.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), 0 < n → R.Represents C → BoundaryVanishes C → (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), R.orient x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x) = 0) → ∀ β γ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (∀ y, (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (n : ℝ) • (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y + fderiv ℝ (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y y) → C γ = 0
